title: Quiz: Measurement System Analysis — Gauge R&R

questions.text: In a Gauge R&R study, 'Repeatability' (Equipment Variation, EV) refers to:
options: Variation between different operators measuring the same part
Variation when the same operator measures the same part multiple times with the same gauge
Variation between different parts measured by the same operator
The combined measurement system error relative to the tolerance
questions.explanation: Repeatability (EV) captures the gauge's own inherent variability: the same operator, same part, same instrument, repeated under identical conditions. If this is large, the instrument itself is unreliable regardless of who uses it.

questions.text: A Gauge R&R study yields %GRR = 18%. According to AIAG MSA Manual thresholds, this measurement system is:
options: Marginal — may be acceptable depending on the application and risk
Unacceptable — exceeds the 10% threshold for acceptance
Excellent — %GRR below 20% always indicates a world-class system
questions.explanation: AIAG thresholds: <10% acceptable, 10–30% marginal, >30% unacceptable. At 18%, the system falls in the marginal zone. Whether to accept it depends on application criticality, cost of alternative systems, and management judgement.

questions.text: In an ANOVA-based Gauge R&R with n=10 parts, k=3 operators, r=2 reps, the degrees of freedom for the Part × Operator interaction are:
questions.explanation: df_PO = (n − 1) × (k − 1) = (10 − 1) × (3 − 1) = 9 × 2 = 18. The interaction term has df equal to the product of the main-effect degrees of freedom.

questions.text: The Number of Distinct Categories (ndc) is calculated as int(√2 × σ_PV / σ_GRR). The AIAG minimum acceptable ndc is:
questions.explanation: AIAG requires ndc ≥ 5. This means the measurement system must be capable of distinguishing at least 5 statistically distinct groups of parts. An ndc of 1 or 2 means the system cannot differentiate parts reliably.

questions.text: A high %Part Variation (PV) in a Gauge R&R study is undesirable because it means the parts differ too much from each other.
questions.explanation: High %PV is actually desirable in a Gauge R&R study. It means the measurement system can distinguish genuine differences between parts — the parts span a wide range relative to the measurement error. If %PV is low, either the parts are nearly identical (a poor study design) or the measurement error is drowning out real part differences.
